title: Nutrition MD · TUMS · February 2024 semester (exam 29 June 2024)
originalFilename: Final exam of nutrition of TUMS, Feb 2024.pdf
scopeNote: Cover says February 2024 semester and Date of Exam Jun29, 2024. Forty questions on PDF pp2–7; p8 is a marked answer sheet, not an authenticated official key. Highlighted selections are preserved as provided marks, with evidence-based editorial corrections and explicitly identified study repairs. Student-identifying header on p8 removed from the public derivative; Downloads original untouched.

questions.prompt: Basal Energy Expenditure (BEE) typically representing ........ percent of Total Energy Expenditure (TEE).
questions.explanation: Basal/resting energy expenditure commonly accounts for roughly 60–70% of total energy expenditure in sedentary adults; the fraction varies with activity and illness.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 166–169 (PDF counter).
questions.note: Approximate teaching range, not a fixed percentage.

questions.prompt: With increasing age Resting Energy Expenditure (REE) will be:
questions.explanation: REE tends to fall with age, importantly through loss of metabolically active lean tissue.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 166–169 (PDF counter).

questions.prompt: Which one is different from the others in terms of Thermic Effect of Food (TEF)?
questions.explanation: Non-exercise activity thermogenesis refers to energy expenditure from daily movement rather than meal processing; the other terms describe TEF.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 166–169 (PDF counter).

questions.prompt: Which one is correct regarding to BMI?
options: In healthy weight person BMI is 18.5–24.9
In healthy weight person BMI is 25–29.9
In extreme obesity BMI is over 30
questions.explanation: The standard adult healthy-weight BMI range is 18.5–24.9 kg/m²; 25–29.9 is overweight and ≥30 is obesity.
evidence: https://www.cdc.gov/bmi/adult-calculator/bmi-categories.html

questions.prompt: In elderly the need of protein and daily energy will:
questions.explanation: Older adults often benefit from a higher protein intake per kilogram while energy expenditure tends to fall. This is a general healthy-ageing teaching point; kidney disease and other illness require individual assessment.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 384–395 (PDF counter).
questions.note: The adult RDA does not automatically change for everyone; geriatric expert recommendations and clinical circumstances matter.

questions.prompt: Which of the following produces 4 kilocalorie per gram?
questions.explanation: Digestible carbohydrate provides about 4 kcal/g. Whole grains are mixed foods including water/fiber and do not necessarily provide exactly 4 kcal per gram of food.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 29–30 (PDF counter).
questions.note: Repaired option C to identify the nutrient rather than misstate a whole food energy density.

originalQuestion.prompt: Which of the following produces 4 kilocalorie per gram?

questions.prompt: In elderly who are complaining of muscle pain which vitamin deficiency is more prominent?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D deficiency may produce muscle weakness and bone/muscle pain. These symptoms are nonspecific, so this is the best exam association, not a diagnosis from pain alone.
evidence: https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/VitaminD-HealthProfessional/

questions.prompt: Which micronutrient deficiency is more related to delayed wound healing and pressure sore development in elderly?
questions.explanation: Zinc deficiency can impair wound healing and immune function. Pressure injury is multifactorial; routine zinc supplementation without a deficiency is not implied.
evidence: https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Zinc-HealthProfessional/

questions.prompt: Which one contains more levels of monounsaturated fatty acid (MUFA)?
questions.explanation: Conventional olive oil is particularly rich in oleic acid and is the intended highest-MUFA choice among ordinary versions of these oils. High-oleic sunflower cultivars can change the ranking.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 83–86 (PDF counter).
questions.note: Assumes conventional oil varieties, not high-oleic sunflower oil.

questions.prompt: Which listed omega-6:omega-3 ratio has the greatest relative proportion of omega-3, without implying that it is a universally optimal dietary target?
questions.explanation: Of the listed ratios, 4:1 contains the greatest relative amount of omega-3. A universally optimal omega-6:omega-3 ratio has not been established; adequate absolute intakes matter.
evidence: https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Omega3FattyAcids-HealthProfessional/
questions.note: Repaired: original claims a universal best health ratio that current ODS guidance does not establish.

originalQuestion.prompt: Which one could be a better ratio of Omega-6:Omega-3 for our health?

questions.prompt: In terms of the definition of malnutrition which one is the best answer?
options: Malnutrition results from low intake of nutrients compared to the body’s needs
Malnutrition results from imbalance between the intake of nutrients and the body’s needs
Malnutrition results from high intake of energy compared to the body’s needs
Malnutrition results from low intake of protein and energy compared to the body’s needs
questions.explanation: Malnutrition includes deficiencies, excesses or imbalances of nutrient/energy intake; the broader imbalance definition is most inclusive.
evidence: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/malnutrition

questions.prompt: Which food is cholesterol free?
questions.explanation: Coconut is a plant food and contains no cholesterol, although coconut fat is high in saturated fatty acids.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 83–94 (PDF counter).

questions.prompt: In Indirect Calorimetry (IC) which items will be quantified?
options: Individual’s nitrogen consumption and carbon dioxide production
Individual’s oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production
Individual’s oxygen consumption and nitrogen production
Individual’s nitrogen consumption and hydrogen production
questions.explanation: Indirect calorimetry estimates energy expenditure from oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production; some equations also account for urinary nitrogen.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 166–167, 428 (PDF counter).

questions.prompt: Which factor is hindering calcium absorption?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D deficiency reduces active calcium absorption; calcitriol normally facilitates it.
evidence: https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Calcium-HealthProfessional/

questions.prompt: In obesity how many kilocalories of energy per day should be restricted to lose one pound of body fat in a week?
questions.explanation: The historical static calculation is 3,500 kcal per pound ÷ 7 days = 500 kcal/day. Real weight change is dynamic and not a guaranteed 1 lb/week response.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 169–174 (PDF counter).
questions.note: Teaching arithmetic only, not a personalized calorie prescription.

questions.prompt: Which clinical sign could be more related to kwashiorkor compared to marasmus?
questions.explanation: Sparse, brittle or depigmented hair is classically associated with kwashiorkor. Edema is its stronger distinguishing feature but is not offered.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 116–118, 426 (PDF counter).

questions.prompt: Which item in Healthy Eating Plate has been considered as the most area of the plate?
questions.explanation: In the Harvard Healthy Eating Plate illustration, vegetables occupy the largest single sector; vegetables and fruits together occupy half the plate.
evidence: https://nutritionsource.hsph.harvard.edu/healthy-eating-plate/

questions.prompt: Which one is digested by colonic bacteria?
questions.explanation: Raffinose reaches the colon because human digestive enzymes cannot cleave its alpha-galactoside linkage. Colonic microbes ferment it. Lactose/fructose can also be fermented when malabsorbed, but not normally as the defining pathway.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 517 (PDF counter).
questions.note: Original option spelling Rafinose retained.

questions.prompt: Which part of GI has no enzyme to digest carbohydrate?
questions.explanation: The stomach does not secrete a carbohydrate-digesting enzyme. Swallowed salivary amylase may continue working transiently until inactivated by gastric acid.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 130–141 (PDF counter).

questions.prompt: Which is the principal apical intestinal facilitated transporter specialized for fructose uptake?
questions.explanation: GLUT5 is the apical intestinal fructose transporter. GLUT2 can also transport fructose, particularly across the basolateral membrane, so the site is specified.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 138–141 (PDF counter).
questions.note: Repaired to specify the apical enterocyte transporter; the original unqualified wording also fits GLUT2.

originalQuestion.prompt: Which one is facilitated transporter for fructose?

questions.prompt: Which part of amino acid does dedicate the amino acid function?
questions.explanation: The variable side chain (R group) largely determines an amino acid’s chemical properties and distinguishes one amino acid from another.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 109–112 (PDF counter).

questions.prompt: Which amino acid is commonly limiting in cereal proteins?
questions.explanation: Lysine is commonly the limiting indispensable amino acid in cereal proteins. Limiting amino acids depend on the protein source; legumes have a different pattern.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 113–115 (PDF counter).
questions.note: Repaired to specify cereal proteins rather than all foods.

originalQuestion.prompt: Which one is the most common limiting amino acid?

questions.prompt: Which statement best reflects current evidence about oral thiamin toxicity?
options: Sensory neuropathy is its characteristic toxicity
No UL is established because adverse-effect data are insufficient
Nausea, jaundice and elevated liver enzymes define its usual toxicity
Numbness or tingling is its characteristic toxicity
questions.explanation: No tolerable upper limit has been set for oral thiamin because adverse-effect data are insufficient. This does not prove that arbitrarily large doses are harmless. Neuropathy is classically associated with excess B6; niacin can cause hepatotoxicity.
evidence: https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Thiamin-HealthProfessional/
questions.note: Repaired the unsafe absolute claim of impossible toxicity.

originalQuestion.prompt: Select the symptom(s) that characterize thiamin toxicity.
options: You can’t consume enough thiamin for it to be toxic
Nausea, jaundice and elevated liver enzymes
Numbness or tingling in the hands, arms and face

questions.prompt: Which condition is described as vitamin D deficiency in adults characterized by a softening of the bones?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D deficiency can impair adult bone mineralization and cause osteomalacia. In children, the growth-plate disorder is rickets.
evidence: https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/VitaminD-HealthProfessional/

questions.prompt: Vitamin C is a water-soluble vitamin. Therefore, which of the following is a true statement?
options: Vitamin C is easily stored in your body for long periods of time
It is easy to consume too much vitamin C and suffer from toxicity
Vitamin C does not need to be replenished regularly
Vitamin C is easily flushed out of your body
questions.explanation: Absorbed excess vitamin C is excreted in urine and regular dietary intake is needed. Water solubility does not make high doses risk-free; gastrointestinal adverse effects can occur.
evidence: https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/VitaminC-HealthProfessional/

questions.prompt: What is the term used to describe a type of anemia in which red blood cells are large and immature, reducing the blood’s ability to transport oxygen?
questions.explanation: Megaloblastic anemia describes impaired DNA synthesis with large erythroid precursors, commonly from folate/B12 deficiency. Pernicious anemia is a particular cause of B12 deficiency, not the general morphological category.
evidence: https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Folate-HealthProfessional/

questions.prompt: Which option is a low-bone-density finding rather than an infant-feeding, obesity or renal-function risk category?
options: Individuals with high body mass index
questions.explanation: Osteopenia is a low-bone-density finding, not proof that vitamin D status is normal. All listed groups can have vitamin D problems, and kidney disease primarily impairs activation. The repaired comparison distinguishes a bone finding from the specified exposure/physiological risk categories.
evidence: https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/VitaminD-HealthProfessional/
questions.note: Original negative risk statement is false: patients with osteopenia are not protected.

originalQuestion.prompt: Which populations are not at risk of vitamin D deficiency?
options: Individuals with high body mass index

questions.prompt: For a pregnant woman with pre-pregnancy BMI of 28 kg/m² the recommended total weight gain is:
questions.explanation: For an overweight prepregnancy BMI and singleton pregnancy, the conventional IOM range is 7–11.5 kg (15–25 lb); 7–11 kg is the closest rounded source option.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 320, Table 11-4 (PDF counter).
questions.note: Singleton pregnancy; source option truncates the upper limit by 0.5 kg.

questions.prompt: Which pair of traditional food groups most directly targets increased protein needs and adequate calcium in pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Dairy and protein-rich foods are conventional ways to meet pregnancy calcium/protein needs. Other nutrient-dense food groups may also increase; vegetarian equivalents can meet requirements.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 314–318 (PDF counter).
questions.note: Original broad question is not exclusive; repaired to specify calcium and protein targets.

originalQuestion.prompt: The intake of which food groups are recommended to be increased in pregnancy compared pre-pregnancy?

questions.prompt: Which nutrient in colostrum is higher than mature breast milk?
questions.explanation: Colostrum is relatively protein-rich, including protective immune proteins, compared with mature milk.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 344–345 (PDF counter).

questions.prompt: Which foods should be avoided for infants during the entire first year of life?
questions.explanation: Current AAP guidance advises no fruit juice before 12 months unless clinically indicated. Well-cooked egg can be introduced with complementary foods; avoiding egg throughout the first year is outdated. The source C mark is corrected to A.
evidence: https://publications.aap.org/pediatrics/article/139/6/e20170967/38754/Fruit-Juice-in-Infants-Children-and-Adolescents
questions.note: Current guidance differs from the marked answer; not an official key.

questions.prompt: Which trio corresponds to the Iranian early-childhood supplementation convention reflected in this paper, with nutrient-specific starting ages rather than all supplements from birth?
options: Vitamin A, vitamin D, vitamin C
questions.explanation: The source reflects Iranian teaching of vitamin A/D plus iron supplementation during infancy/early childhood, with iron starting later. This is not a universal prescription for every infant or all three supplements from birth; timing depends on national policy, feeding and risk.
evidence: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8236148/
questions.note: Repaired to identify the source’s national-policy convention rather than state a global schedule.

originalQuestion.prompt: Which supplements should be given during the first 2 years of life?
options: Vitamin A, vitamin D, vitamin C

questions.prompt: Which option indicates severe malnutrition in the context of injury or acute illness?
questions.explanation: The Academy/ASPEN intake criterion is approximately ≤50% of needs for at least 5 days in acute illness/injury. D also satisfies that numerical threshold, so A and D are accepted. Intake alone is not a complete malnutrition diagnosis.
evidence: https://aspenjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ncp.10310
questions.note: Source has nested true options; do not penalize D.

questions.prompt: Deficiency of which micronutrient can cause petechiae?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C deficiency impairs collagen synthesis and capillary integrity, causing petechiae and perifollicular hemorrhages among other scurvy manifestations.
evidence: https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/VitaminC-HealthProfessional/

questions.prompt: Scaly dermatitis developing during prolonged fat-free parenteral nutrition particularly suggests which deficiency?
questions.explanation: Essential fatty acid deficiency can cause scaly dermatitis, especially during prolonged fat-free nutrition. Flaky nails alone are nonspecific and do not establish EFAD; the study version tests the supported skin/nutrition relationship.
evidence: https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Omega3FattyAcids-HealthProfessional/
DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 87–88 (PDF counter).
questions.note: Repaired nonspecific nail finding to a supported characteristic manifestation.

originalQuestion.prompt: Flaky nails can be caused by which of the following conditions?

questions.prompt: Compared with long-chain triglycerides, why can oral/enteral MCT help when fat digestion and absorption are impaired?
options: It supplies the essential fatty acids
It has uniquely more energy per gram than every other fat
It is already a hydrolyzed oil
It is absorbed more readily with less dependence on bile salts and pancreatic lipase
questions.explanation: Enteral MCT is more readily hydrolyzed/absorbed and less dependent on bile-mediated micellar transport than long-chain fat. MCT is not an essential fatty acid. Intravenous lipid bypasses gut digestion, so the source’s lipid-emulsion context must not be used to claim an enteral mechanism for IV feeding.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 465, 537–538 (PDF counter).
questions.note: Repaired route and absolute option wording; IV emulsions do not undergo intestinal digestion.

originalQuestion.prompt: The benefit of MCT oil that is added to lipid emulsion is:
options: It is an essential fatty acid
It does not require bile salts or pancreatic lipase for digestion

questions.prompt: Which statement about fructooligosaccharides (FOS) is false?
options: They can change short-chain fatty acid concentrations
questions.explanation: FOS fermentation can alter microbiota, short-chain fatty acids and colonic pH and can affect bowel function. The original question has no sound exception; its marked C is not valid. The repaired negative statement makes C the false option.
evidence: https://www.efsa.europa.eu/sites/default/files/topic/ndaart13ref01.pdf
questions.note: Original all-four-effects item explicitly repaired.

originalQuestion.prompt: Fructooligosaccharides (FOS), which have been added to enteral formulas, have these effects, except:
options: Changes in short-chain fatty acid concentrations

questions.prompt: Which is not one of the three characteristic electrolyte decreases used in the ASPEN definition of refeeding syndrome?
questions.explanation: The defining electrolyte declines in ASPEN criteria involve phosphate, potassium and magnesium. Sodium and water retention can also occur, so sodium must not be described as unchanged.
evidence: https://aspenjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ncp.10474
questions.note: Repaired false assertion that sodium never changes.

originalQuestion.prompt: Which ion does not change in refeeding syndrome?

questions.prompt: Which statement incorrectly presents an 8-hour infusion as the usual default schedule for parenteral nutrition?
options: Administration should not exceed 2 g of lipid emulsion per kilogram of body weight per day
The lipid infusion should be discontinued when triglyceride level exceeds 400 mg/dL
PN most often is infused during 8 hours per day with the lipid as part of the PN solution
questions.explanation: PN often starts as a continuous infusion; stable home PN may be cycled, commonly over a longer overnight interval. A universal 8-hour default is not correct. Lipid doses and triglyceride actions vary by formulation and patient; 400 mg/dL often prompts reduction/holding according to protocol, not one universal rule.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 474–481 (PDF counter).
questions.note: Repaired to focus on the incorrect universal infusion schedule rather than present variable lipid limits as universal.

originalQuestion.prompt: Which is not correct about lipid emulsion in parenteral nutrition?
options: Administration should not exceed 2 g of lipid emulsion per kilogram of body weight per day
The lipid infusion should be discontinued when triglyceride level exceeds 400 mg/dL
PN most often is infused during 8 hours per day with the lipid as part of the PN solution

questions.prompt: Which gastric-tube-feeding complication is particularly promoted by insufficient fluid and fiber?
questions.explanation: Constipation can occur with tube feeding, especially when fluid or fiber intake is insufficient. Distension, diarrhea and aspiration are also possible complications, so the original except question has no valid answer.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 472–473 (PDF counter).
https://www.bapen.org.uk/education/nutrition-support/enteral-nutrition/management-of-enteral-feeding-complications/
questions.note: Repaired original false exception; source marked constipation despite it being a recognized complication.

originalQuestion.prompt: Which is not related to signs and symptoms to gastric feeding?
